## Not simply where you can park—but which night is worth remembering

This is not a directory of every car park in Taiwan. A stop stays on the list only when it offers a real reason to go—ocean, lake, sunrise, night views, hot springs, forest, cycling, local culture or family activities—and when we can trace JoyForest photos, official/operator information, or a credible campervan or car-sleeping report.

<div class="overnight-summary-grid" aria-label="Database overview">
  <div><strong>42</strong><span>curated stops</span></div><div><strong>21</strong><span>managed stays</span></div><div><strong>21</strong><span>scenic stops</span></div><div><strong>4</strong><span>travel themes</span></div>
</div>

<div class="callout overnight-safety-callout"><strong>For a first campervan trip:</strong> spend at least half your nights at managed campsites so you can top up water and power, shower and learn the equipment comfortably. Use coasts, parks, harbours and hot-spring parking as the adventurous half of the route. The JoyForest campervan is roughly 5 m long, 2 m wide and 3 m high, so check access, clearance, marked spaces and current overnight rules before arrival. At ordinary parking areas, rest inside the vehicle only—do not deploy awnings, furniture, cooking gear or projection equipment.</div>

<section class="overnight-place-section" id="managed-stays" aria-labelledby="managed-stays-title">
  <div class="overnight-place-section__head"><div><span>50% FORMAL / MANAGED</span><h2 id="managed-stays-title">21 campsites and managed stays</h2></div><p>Best for water, shore power, showers, hot springs or using the full outdoor kit—and the easiest choice for first-time renters.</p></div>
  <div class="overnight-place-grid"><article class="overnight-place-card" id="place-01">
  <a class="overnight-place-card__media" href="https://xn--fiq57vhrvoqqq6v.tw/upload/3d487f8f36a64047c848953df66d7d95.jpg" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" aria-label="View the image source for Taipei｜Huazhong Riverside Campground">

  </a>

    <p class="overnight-place-card__type">🏕️ Campsite / managed stay</p>
    <h3>Taipei｜Huazhong Riverside Campground</h3>
    <p class="overnight-place-card__reason">A practical first night after a Taipei handover, with grass, water, electricity, bathrooms and riverside cycling.</p>
    <div class="overnight-place-card__note"><strong>Before you go:</strong> Official sources list RV pitches, utilities and waste facilities. Confirm which pitch accepts an outside self-drive campervan.</div>

## How to use this list

Choose a travel theme first, then check the map, photo and latest source for each place. Even a formal campground may need advance confirmation that it accepts an outside self-drive campervan around 3 m high. At beaches, harbours, parks and hot-spring parking areas, same-day signs and manager instructions always take priority. If a place is unsuitable, move to a nearby managed campsite rather than forcing the stop.

For a complete route, continue with our [13-day counter-clockwise Taiwan campervan loop](/en/trip-stories/taiwan-counterclockwise-campervan-loop-13-days/). First-time renters should also review [How to use the campervan](/en/pages/booking-guide) and [Availability](/en/pages/availability).
